title: Stakeholders in the workplace
log: 2026-10-29T12:22:32Z write: the API refused it in the chapter request, so it is written on its own next

match.reason: The existing stakeholders point covers stakeholders of a business in general and their clashing interests, while the new point covers the specific human resource stakeholders (unions, employer associations, government bodies) who shape how people are managed, which is a narrower and different idea.

draft.title: Stakeholders in the workplace
card: A stakeholder is any person or group with an interest in how a business manages its people, or who is affected by it. Each one can shape human resource decisions.
Employers set the goals, budgets and policies for managing staff. Employees supply labour and want fair pay, safe conditions and job security.
An employer association represents the interests of businesses, such as by giving advice and speaking to government. A union represents employees, such as by bargaining for pay and conditions.

Government organisations make and enforce the rules that businesses must follow when managing staff. Society, meaning the wider community, expects businesses to treat workers ethically, and can influence a business through its views and buying choices.
draft.remember: Every stakeholder has its own interest in how people are managed, and each can shape the decisions a business makes.

a.q: Which stakeholder mainly acts to represent the interests of employees in bargaining over pay and conditions?
a.why: A union speaks for employees and bargains for them on pay and conditions. An employer association is the tempting wrong answer, because it also represents a group, but that group is businesses, not employees.
a.clue: Which group is made up of workers who join together?

b.q: Several local cafés in Bathurst join a group that gives them advice on staffing and speaks to government about wage costs. Which stakeholder is the group?
b.why: A group of businesses that gives advice and speaks for them on staffing issues is an employer association. It is not a union, because a union represents employees, not business owners.
b.clue: Who are the members of this group: owners or workers?
